text: Figure 7.19: UDS status bit 3 ConfirmedDTC logic The figure is applicable If DemOBDDelayedDCYConfirmedAndMIL is set to false. If DemOBDDelayedDCYConfirmedAndMIL is set to true the confirmed bit transition to 1 dependes further more on the operation cylcle qualification, see [SWS_Dem_01220]. Note: The “AgingCriteriaFulfilled” condition is specified by [SWS_Dem_00498]. The “FaultRecordOverwritten” condition is specified by [SWS_Dem_00409]. The parameter DemEventConfirmationThreshold controls the operation cycle in which the confirmedDTC bit is set based on the first occurrence of the failure. The confirmedDTC bit is always set to 1 when the fault occurs, but the operation cycle in which this is done is depending on the use case. The value is relevant for OEM and legislated requirements on setting the confirmedDTC bit from 0 to 1. In the T able 7.1 below, the most common use cases and necessary values are given: DemEventConfirmationThreshold Use Case 1 The confirmedDTC bit is set from 0 to 1 the first time the testFailed bit is set from 0 to 1. This behavior is also called "immediate confirmation" or "zero trip". This setting is mostly used for non-OBD UDS DTCs. 2 The confirmedDTC bit is set from 0 to 1 in the operation cycle after the failure was reported the first time. This setting is used to fulfill legislated OBD requirements in the US. 3 The confirmedDTC bit is set from 0 to 1 in the second operation cycle after the failure was reported the first time. This setting is used to fulfill legislated OBD requirements in Europe. Table 7.1: Common values for DemEventConfirmationThreshold to solve typical requirements Other OEM specific values for DemEventConfirmationThreshold beside the mentioned values from T able 7.1 are also possible. The parameter DemEventConfirmationThreshold is an AUTOSAR Dem specific threshold value that is by "1" greater than the "trip counter" that is used in ISO 14229- 1:2020[2] figure D.4.
